userStories.title: Reject peer impersonation by binding routed frames to authenticated connId
userStories.description: As the relay, I need ws-default to overwrite `env.from` with the authenticated connection id and forbid peers from spoofing host frames or `to:'all'` from a peer when impersonating another peer.
acceptanceCriteria: Working dir: /Users/tuongaz/dev/seeflow-viewer/cloud
Modify cloud/lambda/share/ws-default.ts `routeFrame`: ALWAYS set `env.from = connId` after findConnRole (do not trust client-supplied `from`)
Add rule: if `found.role === 'peer'` and `env.to === 'host'` -> allowed; if peer and `env.to === 'all'` -> rewrite to `host` (peers cannot fan-out to all peers; only host can broadcast)
Add rule: if `env.type === 'kick'` or `env.type === 'files-manifest'` or `env.type === 'rpc-result'` and `found.role === 'peer'` -> return 403 'host-only-type' and do not forward
Add rule: if `env.to` is a specific connId AND that connId is not present in `session.peers` AND not the `session.hostConnId` -> return 404 'unknown-target' (prevents probing)

Extend cloud/lambda/share/ws-default.test.ts with tests: spoofed `from` is overwritten; peer sending `to:'all'` is rewritten to host (only host receives); peer sending `type:'kick'` returns 403; specific connId that doesn't exist returns 404; host sending `to:'all'` still fans out to every peer

userStories.title: Add abuse-pattern integration test suite
userStories.description: As CI, I need a single integration test file that exercises the abuse patterns end-to-end (flood, oversized frame, replay, peer impersonation, JWT-fail storm, oversized upload, peer-cap, idempotent DDB) against in-process handlers, so regressions are caught before deploy.
acceptanceCriteria: Working dir: /Users/tuongaz/dev/seeflow-viewer/cloud
Create cloud/lambda/share/abuse.it.ts as a bun-test file (`bun test` will discover *.test.ts; rename to abuse.test.ts if needed for discovery)

The file builds a fake DDB store + fake ApiGatewayManagementApiClient (mock `doc.send` via module-level injection or `bun:test` mock), then drives the real handlers from session-create.ts, session-join.ts, ws-default.ts, ws-disconnect.ts

Scenarios (each its own `test()` block): (1) Flood: 200 frames from one peer in <1s -> >0 responses are 429; (2) Oversized frame: 300 KB body -> 413; (3) Replay: same peerJwt used twice -> second auth-peer is 401 replay-detected; (4) Impersonation: peer sends `from: 'fake-host-conn'` -> from is rewritten and host does NOT receive frames addressed `to:'all'`; (5) JWT storm: 1000 random invalid JWTs -> all 401, total runtime under 5s, no DDB writes for invalid JWTs; (6) Oversized upload intent: size = 20 MB -> 413; (7) Peer-cap: 21st peer -> 429 peer-cap-reached; (8) Idempotent DDB: addPeer called twice with same connId yields exactly one entry (UpdateExpression overwrites)
Each test makes its assertion in <500 lines of code total; share a `setupSession()` helper at top of file
Add a script `"test:abuse": "bun test lambda/share/abuse.test.ts"` to cloud/package.json

Rehearsal procedure section: a step-by-step manual test the operator runs quarterly — start a session, post the URL into a private channel, count peers, kick + rotate, verify alarms fire, write findings into a dated subsection at the bottom of the same doc
